findings.description: CON-SUP-107 does not define the program-code integrity method or the reference value against which the result is judged, so the check cannot be reproduced.
findings.requested_change: Define the integrity method and reference value for the start-up program-code check.

findings.description: A failed start-up program-code check cannot be determined until its method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define how failure of the start-up program-code integrity check is determined.

findings.description: The requirement specifies segment size and frequency but does not define how the segment is checked or judged intact.
findings.requested_change: Define the run-time segment-check method and its reference value.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time program-code segment check cannot be determined until the check method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define how failure of the run-time segment check is determined.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-026 do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third supervisor reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify the fault and reset sequence that triggers the latch.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8.
findings.requested_change: Define the entity reported for watchdog-reset fault code 8.

findings.description: Neither SYS-SUP-037 nor CON-SUP-113 defines the permitted values and meanings of the returned state field.
findings.requested_change: Define the supervision states and their representations in the status response.

findings.description: The trigger detects an unfinished execution at the limit while the same requirement permits completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 calls an execution longer than the limit an overrun and also specifies detection at expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the completion boundary and detection instant, then make the trigger and permitted boundary consistent.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the expected configuration CRC.
findings.requested_change: Define the complete CRC variant, covered data range and stored reference representation.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-038 requires eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. CON-SUP-113 does not define that response.
findings.requested_change: Define the response for zero through seven retained reports and reconcile the requirement with that response.

findings.description: The requirement gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold.
findings.requested_change: Specify a verifiable event or maximum response time for driving the status signal high.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it.
findings.requested_change: Define the service-tool mechanism for reading the reset cause and add the corresponding requirements.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the specified safe-state and recovery responses.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and specify the safe-state and recovery response to a detected watchdog-reset fault.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires a start-up configuration fault to latch the safe state. SYS-SUP-009 requires remaining safe until a power-on reset but does not require setting the latch retained across software and watchdog resets by SYS-SUP-028.
findings.requested_change: Specify that a start-up configuration fault sets the safe-state latch with the retention and clearing behavior required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires reset causes to be classified from reset flags. SYS-SUP-031 specifies the classifications but does not require use of the reset flags.
findings.requested_change: Include the required reset-flag basis for reset-cause classification.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-049 requires adding detected fault reports to retained history but specifies no ordering relative to the reset requested by SYS-SUP-024. A reset can therefore occur before the new report is retained, leaving SYS-SUP-038 without that report.
findings.requested_change: Specify when a detected fault report must be committed to retained history relative to recovery reset.
